title: Automated Workflow in Fiji ImageJ for Protein Colocalization Analysis
author: Vikram Aditya

steps.title: Transient transfection of HEK293 cells
steps.instruction: Seed HEK293 cells (ATCC CRL‑1573) and transiently transfect them with the pcDNA3.1(+)-WT‑OATP1B1 plasmid using Lipofectamine 2000 (Thermo Fisher, cat 11668019) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DNA‑Lipofectamine complexes as described in the Lipofectamine 2000 protocol.
Add the complexes to the cells in complete growth medium.
Incubate the cells for 48 h before downstream processing.

steps.title: Immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: At 48 h post‑transfection, fix the cells and stain with primary antibodies rabbit anti‑FLAG (1:100, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat F7425) and mouse anti‑Na/K‑ATPase (1:50, Santa Cruz, cat sc‑21712), followed by secondary Alexa Fluor 594 goat anti‑rabbit (Thermo Fisher, cat A‑11012) and Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti‑mouse (Thermo Fisher, cat A‑11001); counter‑stain nuclei with DAPI (Thermo Fisher, cat D1306).

substeps.instruction: Fix cells with appropriate fixative (e.g., 4 % paraformaldehyde).
Block non‑specific binding (e.g., 5 % BSA in PBS).
Incubate with primary antibodies at the indicated dilutions for the recommended time.
Incubate with the secondary antibodies at the recommended dilution.
Incubate with DAPI (as supplied) for nuclear staining.
Wash and mount coverslips for imaging.

steps.title: Acquire confocal z‑stack images
steps.instruction: Image the stained cells on an FV10i‑LIV confocal microscope using excitation wavelengths 405 nm (DAPI), 473 nm (Alexa Fluor 488), and 559 nm (Alexa Fluor 594); capture images at 1024 × 1024 pixels with a pixel size of 0.207 µm and Z‑slice spacing of 1 µm. Assign channels: C1 = DAPI, C2 = Na/K‑ATPase, C3 = FLAG‑OATP1B1.

substeps.instruction: Set the microscope laser lines to 405 nm, 473 nm, and 559 nm.
Adjust detector settings to avoid saturation.
Acquire a Z‑stack covering the entire cell thickness with 1 µm step size.
Save the raw image files in the microscope’s native format.

steps.title: Convert raw files to TIFF
steps.instruction: Open Fiji ImageJ, select Process → Batch → Convert…, choose the folder containing the raw confocal files as Input, specify a new folder as Output, set Interpolation = None, and click Convert to generate .tiff files compatible with downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Select the Input folder with raw files.
Select the Output folder for the .tiff files.

steps.title: Identify blank Z‑slices (initial JACoP batch)
steps.instruction: Run a batch BIOP JACoP analysis on the .tiff files to obtain Manders M2 values for each Z‑slice and locate slices with zero or NaN values.

substeps.instruction: Open Fiji and run the following macro (General note 2 explains how to run a macro):
run('BIOP JACoP', 'channel_a=2 channel_b=3 threshold_for_channel_a=Otsu threshold_for_channel_b=Otsu set_auto_thresholds_on_stack_histogram get_manders get_fluorogram');
The macro creates a CSV file (AnalysisResults.csv) containing M2 for every Z‑slice of each image.

steps.title: Extract positive Z‑slice ranges
steps.instruction: Run the provided Python script (or the Windows executable 3_filter_z_planes_app.exe) on the CSV from step 5; the tool creates filtered_z_slices.csv listing, for each image, the first and last Z‑slice that have a positive M2 value.

substeps.instruction: • Install Python ≥ 3.7 and the pandas library.
• Execute the script supplied in the manuscript (it reads AnalysisResults.csv, selects slices with M2 > 0, and writes filtered_z_slices.csv).
• Run the .exe (admin rights may be required).
• In the GUI, select AnalysisResults.csv and click Open.
• The program writes positive_z_slices_ranges.csv (identical to filtered_z_slices.csv) in the same folder.

steps.title: Create substack TIFFs
steps.instruction: In Fiji, run the macro below to read filtered_z_slices.csv, open each original .tiff, generate a substack containing only channels 2‑3 and the Z‑slice range identified, and save the substack as a new .tiff file.

substeps.instruction: // Locate csv file with Z‑slice information
csvPath = File.openDialog('Select CSV file with Z‑slice information');
inputDir = getDirectory('Select folder containing TIFF files');
imageNames = newArray(); startSlices = newArray(); endSlices = newArray();
When the macro prompts, select filtered_z_slices.csv and then the folder containing the original .tiff files. The substack files are saved in a new ‘subhyperstacks’ directory.

steps.title: Calculate Manders coefficient on substacks
steps.instruction: Run BIOP JACoP in batch mode on the substack files to obtain the final Manders M2 values for the filtered Z‑range.

substeps.instruction: Open Fiji and execute the following macro:

run('BIOP JACoP', 'channel_a=1 channel_b=2 threshold_for_channel_a=Otsu threshold_for_channel_b=Otsu set_auto_thresholds_on_stack_histogram get_manders get_fluorogram costes_block_size=5 costes_number_of_shuffling=100');

The macro treats channel 1 as Na/K‑ATPase and channel 2 as FLAG‑OATP1B1 (the two channels present in each substack), uses Otsu thresholding, does **not** consider Z‑slices separately, and writes a final CSV (AnalysisResults.csv) and individual report TIFFs to the ‘Results_Filtered’ folder.
